subject: chemistry
question_text: State and explain Dalton's law of partial pressures.

steps.label: The statement
lines: Dalton's law of partial pressures: the total
pressure exerted by a mixture of chemically
non-reacting gases, at a given temperature and
volume, is equal to the sum of the partial
steps.why: The law only holds when the gases do not react — a reaction would change the number of molecules and the pressure. Non-reacting, and at the same T and V, are therefore part of the statement itself.
common_mistakes: Leaving out chemically non-reacting. HCl and NH₃ in one vessel do not obey this law.
Saying sum of the volumes instead of sum of the partial pressures.
steps.memory_tip: Each gas presses as if it were alone; the mixture's pressure is the sum of those alone-pressures.
steps.margin_note: Non-reacting and same T, V are the two conditions the examiner checks for.

steps.label: The explanation
lines: The partial pressure of a gas is the pressure
that gas would exert if it alone occupied the
whole vessel at the same temperature.
steps.why: The equation needs the term it uses defined: partial pressure is an alone-in-the-vessel pressure. With that meaning fixed, the law is one addition.
common_mistakes: Using the equation without defining partial pressure. The definition is part of this step's mark.
Writing the partial pressure as the gas's pressure in its own separate small container. It fills the WHOLE vessel.
steps.memory_tip: Partial pressure: same vessel, same temperature, the other gases removed.
steps.margin_note: Equation plus the one-sentence definition of partial pressure earn this mark.

steps.label: Partial pressure and mole fraction
lines: For each gas alone in the vessel: pᵢ = nᵢRT / V
Dividing: pᵢ / P = nᵢ / n = xᵢ (mole fraction)
steps.why: Each gas obeys the ideal gas equation on its own, and RT/V is common to all of them, so pressures add exactly as moles add. Dividing one gas's pressure by the total cancels RT/V and leaves the mole fraction.
common_mistakes: Defining mole fraction as nᵢ over the OTHER gases' moles. It is nᵢ over the TOTAL moles n.
Stopping at P = nRT/V without the division that produces pᵢ = xᵢP.
steps.memory_tip: Share of moles = share of pressure: a gas holding one quarter of the moles exerts one quarter of the total pressure.
steps.margin_note: The boxed relation pᵢ = xᵢP is the useful output; the three lines above justify it.

s2_equation.label: The equation
lines: where p₁, p₂, p₃ … are the partial pressures
The partial pressure of a gas is the pressure
that gas would exert if it alone occupied the

s2_equation.margin_note: At 2 marks the statement and the equation complete the answer; the mole-fraction derivation belongs to the 4-mark form.

cuts.note: The book's VSAQ 23 (asked in 2011 and 2014) asks only the statement and the equation; the mole-fraction step is hidden in this cut.

insider_note: Asked repeatedly — 2011 and twice in 2014. The phrase chemically non-reacting gases is the first thing the examiner looks for in the statement.
